UPD-1 (F3): after 'update --fork --latest' fails the feed checksum (exit 13), the unverified Fork stays installed in current\ and starts on the next 'fork'. Fix: restore the 'before update' snapshot automatically, or refuse to launch it (commands/update.py _install_fork).

UPD-2 (F8/F11/F14): _install_fork takes the 'before update' snapshot before downloading the installer. A failed or offline attempt leaves an extra snapshot of the installed version; with keep=2 the next launch's prune then deletes the only snapshot of the previous version, which is the rollback target.

UPD-3 (F10): procs._is_fork ignores Velopack's Update.exe. During the roughly 4 s of 'Restart and Update', fork, rollback, update --fork and setup treat Fork as closed and can snapshot a half-replaced current\ or start a second Fork.exe.

UPD-4 (A4): a Wine pin change picked up by a normal launch (app upgrade, or 'config set wine.build') re-runs wine_runtime and prefix_init but never stops the old build's wineserver; only 'update --wine' does. Not yet reproduced; the planned test will confirm it.
UPD-5 (A8): state.json does not record which fork-linux version wrote it, so a downgrade cannot warn.

UPD-6 (F3): the trust-on-first-use check is weaker in setup than in update. 'setup --fork-version V --allow-untested' (steps/fork.py _verify_tofu) only warns when the feed does not list V, while 'update --fork' refuses with exit 13; AGENTS.md hard rule 6 requires the checksum to match.
UPD-7 (A14): install.sh deletes the old install directory before copying the new one, so an upgrade interrupted in between leaves no working install.
UPD-8 (A2): the 'upgrade in place' step of packaging-e2e-install.sh reinstalls the same artifact, so no real version upgrade is tested in any packaging format yet.
